subject: insurance is the silent killer
preheader: premiums up 10-15 percent a year. florida is the warning.
headline: Insurance line items don't just creep up. They jump.
body: Insurance for investment properties is rising 10-15% per year nationally, and that's the average. Florida coastal counties are up 30-50% in two years. Texas wind/hail zones are up 25%. Even quiet markets like Indianapolis are seeing 8-12% annual increases.

Why it matters for underwriting: a $1,800/yr insurance premium today becomes $2,500-3,000 in five years if your market is on a bad trend line. That's $1,000+ of NOI erosion. On a 6% cap, that's $16,000 of value loss. Not catastrophic, but enough to turn a 'fine' deal into a 'meh' one.

Florida is the canary. Some properties are now genuinely uninsurable through standard carriers — owners are paying $8,000-15,000/yr where it was $2,500 five years ago. The deals don't pencil at all. Investors are quietly exiting whole counties.

What to do: get a real insurance quote before you close, not a rough estimate. Model the premium growing 8-10% per year in your 10-year projection. If the property is in a wind, flood, or wildfire zone, get two quotes and use the higher one.

TrueCap estimates insurance by state and adjusts upward for high-risk regions. Florida coastal, Texas wind, California wildfire — all get bumped. You can override the number, but the default leans honest.
